items.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009
items.q: Max Roach and Art Blakey and Elvin Jones, you know that changed my way of playing

ctx.x: And eventually, did people tell you, you have to go to New York? Or did you just sort of sense that that was where —

Well I mean that’s where it was. Because I used to go to New York all the time. You know I would just get in the car and drive there. And catch a bus and go there. And I knew a lot of musicians in New York. But actually I had — one night John Coltrane was playing at this club in Philly called The Showboat, it was on Lombard Street, down your way. 15th and Lombard. And I was there and I was a pretty experienced drummer at that time. And I was bugging him to let me sit in and play with him, although Elvin was…
And how were you thinking? He said they were thinking like you were.

items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I didn’t get along with Rashied that well... we were playing at The Village Gate... if we are going to play together we have to be coordinated.

ctx.x: When did you leave John Coltrane?

1966. I didn’t get along with Rashied that well. First thing, I don’t know what he was thinking about, but we were playing at The Village Gate and I always went early to get set up so I knew everything. When I went out and came back, when it’s almost time to start, he’s moved my drums and put his all over. I said, “What are you doing here?” We had that going. I said, “Well if we are going to play together we have to be coordinated. Otherwise it’s going to sound like it’s just a mess.”
